column1: Alejandro LERENA
# *** 1. JUSTINIANA LENGUAS AND SIXTA LENGUAS ARE SISTERS. ***
# These acts name Justiniana's parents as PEDRO LENGUAS and CARMEN GONZALEZ - and one of them calls
# him "el GENERAL D. Pedro Lenguas". Sixta Lenguas's own death registration (Montevideo, 17 January
# 1884) names her parents as "Pedro Lenguas, Carmen Gonzalez" and her husband as "Candido Juanico".
# Same parents. So:
#   - Justiniana Lenguas married Luis Lerena, and bore Luis Eugenio and Gilberto.
#   - Her sister SIXTA married CANDIDO JUANICO in 1857, as his second wife.
#   - In December 1864 Luis Eugenio married Candido's daughter JULIA, by his FIRST wife.
# *** So when that marriage was made, the groom's maternal AUNT was already the bride's STEPMOTHER. ***
# The two families were joined seven years before the wedding this archive has treated as the join.
# *** 2. LUIS EUGENIO WAS BORN 9 FEBRUARY 1843 *** - his death act of 1901 gave his age as 56, which
# would put it at 1845. The act of his own baptism is the better evidence.
# ================== AND A CONFLICT, OPENED AND THEN RESOLVED ==================
# *** 3. THE 1846 ACTS NAME LUIS LERENA'S FATHER AS "FRANCISCO". THE 1850 ACT NAMES HIM "SANCHO". ***
# This archive's apex ancestor is SANCHO LLERENA AGUILAR, the Andalusian soldier of the Montevideo
# census, and the line to him runs through Luis Lerena. On the 1846 acts alone that apex looked wrong.
# So the decisive record was opened the same hour rather than left as a doubt: the baptism of
# ALBERTO OCTAVIO LERENA, 7 October 1850, S. Agustin, pueblo de la Restauracion - image ark
# 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZSZQ-J, act No. 585. It reads:
#   "hijo legitimo de D. Luis Lerena y D. Justiniana Lenguas, naturales de Montevideo.
#    *** PATERNOS: D. SANCHO y D. MARIA FERNANDEZ. *** Maternos: D. Pedro y D. Carmen Gonzalez.
#    Padrinos: D. Felipe Lenguas y D. Dominga Carvallo."
# *** SO SANCHO STANDS, and he now stands on an ACT rather than on an index and a published tree. ***
# That is a real upgrade: this archive had marked the whole descent from Sancho as SECONDARY.
# WHY THE 1846 ACTS DISAGREE, and why they lose. They are not original entries. Each ends
# "asi consta del Legajo conservado en este Archivo, mandado trasladar por el Sr. Obispo y Vic.
# Ap. D. Jacinto Vera" - they are LATER TRANSCRIPTS copied out of a legajo by Manuel Madruga, at one
# remove from whatever was written in 1843 and 1846. The 1850 act is a contemporaneous entry in the
# parish's own book. A copy and an original disagreeing is a copy being wrong.
# Everything else in the two sets agrees exactly - the parents, the maternal grandparents Pedro and
# Carmen Gonzalez, the mother Maria Fernandez. Only the paternal grandfather's forename moves.
# *** RECORDED RATHER THAN TIDIED AWAY, *** because the same hand that wrote "Francisco" twice may
# have been copying something, and a future reader meeting a FRANCISCO LERENA in the Montevideo
# registers should know this is where the name came from.
# Also recovered from the 1850 act: the child is ALBERTO OCTAVIO, not "Alberto Otario" as indexed;
# he was born 22 March 1850; his parents are stated "naturales de MONTEVIDEO"; and his godparents
# were D. Felipe Lenguas and Dona Dominga Carvallo - a fourth Lenguas, and a new surname.
